mainEntity.name: What is Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal is a sacred circuit covering three temples - Maa Vindhyavasini (Lakshmi), Kali Khoh (Mahakali), and Ashtabhuja (Mahasaraswati) - forming a holy triangle. This 8-kilometer spiritual journey represents complete worship of divine feminine energy.

mainEntity.name: How long does Trikon Parikrama take in Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal takes 3-4 hours on foot (Pad Parikrama) or 1-2 hours by vehicle. The complete circuit covers approximately 8 kilometers and includes visits to multiple smaller temples along the route.

mainEntity.name: What is the correct route for Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The traditional Trikon Parikrama route in Vindhyachal starts at Maa Vindhyavasini Temple, proceeds to Kali Khoh Temple (2 km), then to Ashtabhuja Temple (3 km from main temple), and returns to complete the sacred triangle circuit.

mainEntity.name: Which temples are included in Trikon Parikrama Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal includes three main temples: Maa Vindhyavasini Temple (representing Goddess Lakshmi), Kali Khoh Temple (Goddess Mahakali), and Ashtabhuja Temple (Goddess Mahasaraswati), along with several smaller temples en route.

mainEntity.name: Can Trikon Parikrama be done by vehicle in Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal can be completed by vehicle for those with physical limitations. However, performing it on foot (Pad Parikrama) is considered more meritorious and spiritually beneficial.

mainEntity.name: What is the best time to do Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best time for Trikon Parikrama in Vindhyachal is early morning (5:00-8:00 AM) or evening (4:00-7:00 PM). During Navratri, late night parikrama (10:00 PM-3:00 AM) offers a unique spiritual experience with fewer crowds.
